$comment: Per-file, sha256-pinned waivers of expand-lint rules for LOCKED files the lint refuses (suite.mjs section 2c). Not the baseline: the baseline is write-once and maps only pre-header files. A waiver is voided by any byte change (the lock pins the file anyway), may name only WAIVABLE_RULES, and is stale-checked (a waived rule that no longer fires fails). A new file never gets one by default: fix the file while it is unlocked.

waivers.reason: SECURITY DEFINER functions of the operator control plane: REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION .. FROM PUBLIC on functions this same file creates is mandatory hardening (Postgres grants EXECUTE to PUBLIC by default) and only tightens an object no colour has seen; the file creates every table it touches (no lock on a live relation), so no lock_timeout is needed. Locked at 0009 before the lint covered the platform chain; its bytes cannot gain a SET.

Replaces the 0009 SECURITY DEFINER guard/queue functions (same signatures, privileges unchanged) and widens one CHECK on plt.provisioning_request (DROP+ADD of provisioning_request_args_check, only ever loosened for import_members) in the platform database, whose sole readers are the operator panel and host executor, deployed together from one release. The purge helper's REVOKE FROM PUBLIC is on a function this file creates. Locked at 0010 before the lint covered the platform chain; its bytes cannot gain a SET or NOT VALID.

Replaces the 0010 SECURITY DEFINER lease functions plt.renew_provisioning_lease and plt.claim_provisioning_request in place with unchanged signatures (create-harden H4: a lapsed lease cannot be renewed and is requeued only after a 60 s grace); CREATE OR REPLACE is the only way to change a function body while keeping the grants pg.ts issues. The file sets lock_timeout first.

SECURITY DEFINER functions of the access record: REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION .. FROM PUBLIC on functions this same file creates is mandatory hardening (Postgres grants EXECUTE to PUBLIC by default) and only tightens objects no colour has seen. The file sets lock_timeout first and creates every relation it touches.
